stem: A nurse educator discusses the historical development of Universal Precautions. Which statement is accurate?

options.A: Universal Precautions developed during the HIV/AIDS era and applied blood and specified body-fluid precautions to all patients regardless of known infection status.
options.B: Universal Precautions began as a food-safety program and were later transferred to hospitals to address occupational blood exposure.
options.C: Universal Precautions required isolation of every hospitalized patient regardless of diagnosis, symptoms, or anticipated blood exposure.
options.D: Universal Precautions replaced hand hygiene and personal protective equipment with environmental disinfection as the principal control.

rationale: CDC's historical isolation-guideline table identifies Universal Precautions in 1985–1988 as having developed in response to the HIV/AIDS epidemic and applying Blood and Body Fluid precautions to all patients regardless of infection status. It also included PPE, handwashing, and sharps recommendations. A is correct.
educational_objective: Recognize the historical purpose of Universal Precautions: blood/body-fluid precautions applied regardless of a patient's known bloodborne infection status during the HIV/AIDS era.

source_original.stem: A nurse educator discusses the historical development of Universal Precautions. Which statement is accurate?

options.A: Universal Precautions developed during the HIV/AIDS era and treated blood and specified body fluids as potentially infectious regardless of known patient status.
options.B: Universal Precautions began as a food-safety program and were later transferred to hospitals to address occupational blood exposure.
options.C: Universal Precautions required isolation of every hospitalized patient regardless of diagnosis, symptoms, or anticipated blood exposure.
options.D: Universal Precautions replaced hand hygiene and personal protective equipment with environmental disinfection as the principal control.

source_original.rationale: CDC’s historical timeline describes Universal Precautions, developed in 1985–1988 in response to HIV/AIDS, as a blood/body-fluid approach applied regardless of known infection status; later concepts were incorporated into Standard Precautions.
source_original.source_detail: Appendix A, Table 1 — 1985–1988 Universal Precautions row. CDC page updated 2023-11-27; currentness rechecked 2026-08-15. NCSBN first-check: Overview of Content — Safety and Infection Prevention and Control, printed p.8: infection prevention, biohazard handling, security plans, equipment safety and workplace safety. 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan; effective 2026-04-01 through 2029-03-31; currentness rechecked 2026-08-15.

correction_summary: Retained the historical Universal Precautions construct and key A, aligned wording to CDC's exact 'all patients regardless of infection status' formulation, and preserved easy difficulty.

audit_findings.source_authority: CDC infection-control historical guidance; NCSBN 2026 Test Plan
audit_findings.exact_locator: Appendix A Table 1, 1985–88 Universal Precautions row
audit_findings.claim_audit: Final item accurately represents the historical CDC description without conflating Universal Precautions with full patient isolation or modern Standard Precautions.

distractor_audit.B: Incorrect; Universal Precautions arose in healthcare in response to HIV/AIDS, not food safety.
distractor_audit.C: Incorrect; the approach concerned specified blood/body-fluid precautions, not universal patient isolation.
distractor_audit.D: Incorrect; PPE and handwashing were components, not replaced by environmental disinfection.

audit_findings.ambiguity_second_answer: Only A matches the CDC historical record.
audit_findings.cueing: All alternatives are historical descriptions of the same infection-control concept.
audit_findings.blueprint: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control — infection-prevention principles.
audit_findings.independent_second_pass: Re-read the CDC historical table and corroborating 1987/1988 MMWR context, all options, rationale and NCSBN mapping. A remained uniquely correct.
